answer: Each new agent identity must post a bond escrowed on-chain and slashed on proven fraud, so one extra sybil costs a full bond instead of a free signup. Since every bond needs a fresh proof of work, the marginal cost of a thousand fakes scales linearly while reward per identity stays flat. That gap makes a sybil flood a negative expected value bet. Honest agents recover their bond at the end of each epoch's horizon with no fraud, and any duplicate crystal of identity data fails the uniqueness signal and forfeits the stake.
